undetermined_behaviors: Pair ordering — determined differently: format.md ('Pairs appear in the encoded line in the order in which they appear in the mapping.') requires mapping/insertion order, while reference.py emits pairs sorted by key (for k in sorted(d)). Exercised by probes 1, 5 and 6, whose insertion order differs from sorted key order (e.g. probe 1: format-faithful 'z=9;a=1' vs reference 'a=1;z=9').

Backslash handling — determined differently (at minimum, not determined to match): format.md's escaping clause ('Inside keys and values, every ';' is written as the two characters backslash-semicolon and every '=' as backslash-equals') names only ';' and '=' as transformed characters, so under its literal reading a backslash passes through unchanged; reference.py additionally doubles every literal backslash (s.replace('\', '\\') applied first). Exercised by probe 4, value 'back\slash': format-faithful 'k=back\slash' vs reference 'k=back\\slash'.

No other behavior exercised by the probe set is undetermined or determined differently: key=value pair rendering, ';' joining, escaping of '=' in keys and values, escaping of ';' including trailing position, empty-key and empty-value rendering, and empty-mapping-to-empty-line are each determined by format.md identically to reference.py; see behavior-statement.md for the clause-by-clause argument.
